chapter_title: There is no Joy that shall remain in the World til

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
No one in the created order can remain in a settled conjunction of good and truth in such a mixed state that full blessedness endures without interruption to the completion.

Even the universal powers that give light to understanding and warmth to love are held in their appointed order without compulsion, for they do not resist the rule above them; yet they too cannot be in unbroken fullness of delight while opposition still stands within the domain.

For there is a first grief: discernment looks steadily upon the reigning evil, perceives it, and sees its repulsive forms. It recognizes that this evil is active and confirmed, exercising dominion in inward and outward things, secretly and openly, doing all it wills from its own love.

And there is a second grief: discernment perceives the living spiritual principle and sees it caught under a great constraint in inner and outer degrees, held within perverted perception and within corrupt life, bound by continual oppression. It is pressed, drawn into proximity, divided and consumed as it rises and falls through states; it is driven from higher to lower and from lower to higher, stripped of coverings and carried from one external form to another.

Because this living spiritual principle is loved and held in reverence, those who love it cannot rejoice completely while they behold it under such oppression.

Thus there is sorrow both for the captive life within, and for the hostile evil seen ruling what is not its own. That evil exults and is satisfied with good and truth it has seized as if they were its possession. Therefore joy is not yet total, but there is endurance and inward restraint until the living spiritual principle is purified and taken out of the enemy’s dominion. Then the intention of spiritual death, which is the enemy, is deprived of its power and confined so it cannot go forth again.

When, at the completion, the enemy is finally bound so it cannot act, joy becomes full and grief no longer returns. Then the state is restored in permanence to what it was in its first purity, to eternity.

paragraph_translations.translation: No one within the created order can remain in a settled conjunction of good and truth while still in a mixed state, so that full blessedness endures without interruption to the completion.
paragraph_translations.connection: OPENS the chapter by stating the impossibility of lasting joy in a mixed state.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Standing firm in mixture” forced as a state of unstable conjunction while good and evil (or truth and falsity) remain mingled.

paragraph_translations.translation: Even the universal powers that illuminate understanding and warm affection are maintained in their appointed order without being driven by oppression, since they do not resist the rule that summons them into use and holds them in obedience; yet even these cannot be in complete rejoicing.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS the claim by extending it from individuals to universal governing powers.
paragraph_translations.notes: The phrasing about being “set firm in a summons and an obedience” is awkward; rendered as orderly responsiveness to higher rule.

paragraph_translations.translation: This is the first cause: discernment fixes its attention on the reigning evil, perceives it, and beholds its repulsive forms. It sees that this evil is active and confirmed, exercising dominion in inner and outer things, secretly and openly, doing everything it desires from its own love.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by giving the first reason joy cannot be complete.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Eyes” treated as discernment; “ugly shapes” as repulsive forms of evil.

paragraph_translations.translation: The second cause: discernment perceives the living spiritual principle and sees it ensnared under a great constraint in inner and outer degrees, held within perverted perception and within corrupt life, bound by every kind of oppression. It is pressed, drawn into proximity, divided and consumed as it rises and falls through states, driven from higher to lower and from lower to higher, stripped of its coverings and carried from one external form to another.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by adding the second reason: the life within is oppressed and displaced.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Tree and flesh” required a best-fit rendering as perverted perception and corrupt life; “sliced and eaten” forced as being divided and made subservient/consumed.

paragraph_translations.translation: Because this living spiritual principle is loved and held in reverence, those who love it cannot rejoice completely when they see it under oppression.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES by drawing the emotional consequence from the second cause.

paragraph_translations.translation: So there is sorrow for the living spiritual principle, and sorrow for the enemy seen ruling what is not its own. The enemy is proud and satisfied with good and truth it has seized as its wealth. For this reason joy is not yet total, but there is endurance and inward restraint until the living spiritual principle is purified and taken out of the enemy’s dominion. Then the intention of spiritual death, which is the enemy, is deprived of its power and confined permanently so it cannot go forth into life.
paragraph_translations.connection: SHIFTS from diagnosis to the process of deliverance and the fate of the enemy.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Swallow their heart” treated as inward restraint; “shut it up in the lump” is unclear—rendered as permanent confinement and removal from operation.

paragraph_translations.translation: When, at the completion, the enemy is finally bound so it cannot act, then they rejoice and grief ceases from that point. They are restored forever to the same state they were in at the beginning.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONCLUDES by stating the final binding of evil and restoration of the first state.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Bond at the last” taken as final restraint at the completion of the process.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Strongly coherent as a single spiritual teaching: lasting joy is impossible while evil still rules and the living spiritual principle remains bound; endurance continues until purification, liberation, and the final restraint of the enemy, after which the original pure state is restored. The only stumbles are a few opaque idioms (“shut it up in the lump,” “tree and flesh,” “sliced and eaten”), which required interpretive but consistent spiritual renderings.

findings.diagnosis: Clean opening thesis in correspondential mode: joy cannot remain while existence is ‘standing firm in mixture.’ No administrative overlay; the statement sets a functional/spiritual condition (mixture → unstable joy).
findings.evidence: Text: “There is not [o]ne person… standing firm [i]n mixture, for whom joy remains to the end.” The spiritual reading notes only a mild forcing (“Standing firm in mixture” as an unstable conjunction) but the narrative logic is intact: mixture functionally prevents lasting joy.

findings.diagnosis: Minor idiomatic/lexical difficulty (institutional phrasing) but not a true voice-insertion. The line reads like a Manichaean cosmic-regularity claim applied to sun/moon; ‘summons and obedience’ is awkward yet still functions as a description of ordered responsiveness, not a jurisdictional inventory.
findings.evidence: Text: “they know not [to be set]et firm in a summons and an [obe]dience.” The spiritual reading explicitly stumbled here: “awkward; rendered as orderly responsiveness to higher rule.” However, the passage does not introduce named officials, ranks, stations, or territorial authority; it extends the thesis from humans to cosmic light-givers and keeps the chapter’s argumentative flow (even they cannot rejoice completely).

findings.diagnosis: Clean twofold correspondential teaching (first grief/second grief) with functional spiritual psychology: seeing the enemy’s activity and seeing the soul’s captivity causes incomplete joy. No narrative break; the two reasons are tightly integrated and develop the chapter’s thesis.
findings.evidence: Text: “So, one: Their eyes stare at their enemy…” (¶3) and “The [s]econd: They perceive the living soul…” (¶4) followed by the affective consequence (¶5). The spiritual reading’s mappings (“eyes”→discernment) are straightforward correspondential moves. The noted stumbles (“tree and flesh,” “sliced and eaten”) are opaque imagery but they intensify the same captivity motif rather than diverting into governance lists or alien personnel.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty from dense, possibly damaged or culturally-specific captivity imagery (‘tree and flesh’, ‘sliced and eaten’). The reader had to ‘best-fit’ these phrases, but removing them would not improve coherence; they are the concrete images carrying the correspondential point (the soul is processed/consumed through cycles).
findings.evidence: Text: “in the tree and in the flesh, [bound] with every oppression… sliced and eaten… moved from body to body.” The spiritual reading admits forcing: “‘Tree and flesh’ required a best-fit rendering…; ‘sliced and eaten’ forced…” Yet the surrounding lines (“ensnared… fetter… pressed… eaten… moved from body to body”) all cohere as one captivity-and-transmigration description. No voice boundary marker (‘also, at that time’) or administrative taxonomy appears.

findings.diagnosis: Idiomatic seam (‘swallow their heart’; ‘shut it up in the lump’) but still continuous with the chapter’s deliverance arc. No administrative overlay: the passage keeps agency with the same actors (‘they’ = the light-givers) and continues the functional narrative (endure → cleanse soul → remove from enemy → bind/deactivate death).
findings.evidence: Text: “bear up and swallow their heart… Then they obliterate the death… and they gather it in [and shut it up in the lump] for ever.” The spiritual reading flags the stumbles: “‘Swallow their heart’ treated as inward restraint; ‘shut it up in the lump’ is unclear.” Nevertheless, the sequence is narratively necessary: incomplete joy persists “until they cleanse the living soul… Then…” leading naturally into ¶7’s final binding. There is no shift into named jurisdictions or inventories; the difficulty is idiom, not an inserted administrative block.

findings.diagnosis: Clean conclusion: final binding of the enemy and restoration to the primordial state. This resolves the opening thesis and the two griefs without introducing foreign material.
findings.evidence: Text: “When they will chain their enemy in the bond at the [las]t, then they will rejoice… Also, they become the very same as they were from the [start] for ever!” The spiritual reading reports a smooth conclusion and stable narrative closure.

textual_criticism.summary: No clear textual insertions or administrative overlay blocks detected. The chapter is largely coherent correspondential teaching with a few localized idiomatic/damaged-image stumbles (¶2, ¶4, ¶6). Recommendations: 0 excisions, 0 annotations, 7 ‘none’ (with ¶4 best treated as genuine difficulty/damage in imagery, not an insertion).

harmonized_paragraphs.text: There is not [o]ne person [existing in] the world, standing firm [i]n mixture, for whom joy remains to the end.

Not only people, even the sun and the moon, the light-givers of the heavens, [are set in their courses] nor are they oppressed, they know not [to be set]et firm in a summons and an [obe]dience. Nevertheless, they too, they do not rejoice completely.

So, one: Their eyes stare at their enemy, they [perceiv]e him and also look at his ugly shapes. They [s]ee him, that he is alive and established and is king above and below, in secret and manifest. He does every thing that he wants according to his wil[l].

[The s]econd: They perceive the living soul, they see [i]t and that it is ensnared and set in a great [fetter] above and below, in the tree and in the flesh, [bound] with every oppression. It is being pressed, drawn near to [and] sliced and eaten as it comes up and down; from above below and from below above. It [is] despoiled and moved from body to body.
Now, because of their living soul that is loved by them and honoured of them, when they see it in oppression th[ey can] not [re]joice completely.

So, one about the soul; and one about their enemy whom they see ruling [in] what is not his own. He is proud and satisfied with a wealth that is not his own. Indeed, due to this, they do not rejoice in total; but bear up and swallow their heart until they cleanse the living soul and take it from the enemy's hands. Then they obliterate the death that is their enemy and they gather it in [and shut it up in the lump] for ever and ever.
When they will chain their enemy in the bond at the [las]t, then they will rejoice and no longer grieve from this t[ime]. Also, they become the very same as they were from the [start] for ever!

changes_summary: No changes made. The textual criticism findings recommended no excisions or annotations for ¶1–¶7 (Findings 1–6: all ‘none’).
